To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression of hGH and hPRL in E. coli can be successfully performed using a cIts(-)-lambdaP(L) promoter-controlled expression system, but that the optimal expression conditions are different for the two hormones, with temperature being the main parameter that influences expression.

(a) hPRL can be produced in E. coli, in the periplasm, at yields higher than ever reported; (b) hGH and hPRL are produced under the control of lambdaP(L) with distinct behaviors; (c) the temperature plays a major, but not exclusive, role in the yields obtained.
hGH and hPRL can be successfully expressed in E. coli periplasm using the same expression system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimization of a recombinant expression process in which the promoter is temperature induced, and the results obtained are relevant for the production of recombinant proteins for therapy.
the optimization of a recombinant system to produce hPRL, which is an important therapeutic protein for the treatment of infertility, lactation, and amenorrhea.
the optimization of the production of two human hormones, hGH and hPRL, using the same expression system, and with the identification of the main variables that influence the final protein yields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lambdaP(L) system is not suitable for the production of human prolactin.
temperature, in addition to being a crucial factor for hGH secretion, plays a major role on the yields of hPRL.
temperature is the most important variable in the production of recombinant proteins by lambda PL promoter-controlled systems, and it should be optimized for each protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the temperature plays a major and often underestimated role in the expression of proteins in recombinant E. coli.
the temperature shift method, although useful for some proteins, is not a universal method for the expression of all recombinant proteins in E. coli.
, when using a cIts(-)-based expression system for hPRL, temperature is a major factor that determines the amount of protein obtained.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in order to obtain substantial amounts (i.e., >1 microg ml-1 A(600)-1) of a labile protein from E. coli periplasm via temperature induction, the temperature of induction must be lower than 37 degrees C.
the expression and secretion of hPRL and hGH are not equally feasible under lambdaPL promoter control.
, when using lambdaP(L), temperature plays a crucial role in protein yields.
